name: Fewster-Ford-Roman, 'Probability distributions of smeared quantum stress tensors', arXiv:1004.0179v2 (22 May 2010; PRD 81, 121901(R)), footnote [18]: for self-adjoint A, (a) <psi|A psi> >= -Q on D(A) <=> (b) sigma(A) in [-Q,oo) <=> (c) supp mu_psi in [-Q,oo); spectrum = vacuum support for local A in Minkowski AQFT (Reeh-Schlieder)

published_statement: Note [18] (pp. 8-9): 'The connection begins with the observation that the following three statements are equivalent, where A is a self-adjoint operator (with domain D(A) and spectrum sigma(A)) representing a quantum observable: (a) <psi | A psi> >= -Q for all normalised psi in D(A); (b) sigma(A) subset [-Q, oo); (c) the probability measure mu_psi that describes the distribution of individual measurement results of A in state psi has support supp mu_psi subset [-Q, oo). [The implication (a) => (b) is the Rayleigh-Ritz variational principle; (b) => (c) because measurements always give values in the spectrum; (c) => (a) because any random variable taking values in [-Q, oo) has its expected value in that range.] In general, supp mu_psi (for a fixed choice of psi) can be a proper subset of sigma(A), and in particular the infimum of the support of mu_psi can exceed inf sigma(A). ... However, the spectrum and the support of the probability measure coincide if A is a local observable, such as a smeared field, and psi is the vacuum state Omega of a Minkowski space QFT obeying the standard assumptions of algebraic quantum field theory [11]. ... In particular, sigma(A) and supp mu_Omega have a common infimum, which provides a sharp quantum inequality bound <psi | A psi> >= inf supp mu_Omega for all normalized psi in D(A).' Body, p. 2: 'These lower bounds represent the lowest eigenvalues of the smeared operators. As a consequence of the Reeh-Schlieder theorem ..., they are also the lower bounds of the support of the corresponding probability distributions in the vacuum state [18].'
published_hypotheses: N1 A is SELF-ADJOINT (a symmetric operator on a dense domain is not enough); D(A) is its domain
N2 (a) holds for ALL normalised psi in D(A) -- a state-independent bound Q on the whole domain of that self-adjoint operator
N3 mu_psi is the spectral measure <psi, P_A(.) psi> (the Born-rule distribution of individual outcomes) -- 'distribution' means the quantum spectral measure
N4 the three-way equivalence is abstract Hilbert-space operator theory: no spacetime, dimension, field or state hypothesis
N5 (c) for ONE fixed psi does not give (b): the equivalence is with (c) for every psi (the note's own caveat: inf supp mu_psi can exceed inf sigma(A))
N6 spectrum = support (hence sharpness of the bound) ONLY for A local and psi the vacuum of a MINKOWSKI QFT obeying the AQFT axioms (Reeh-Schlieder)

N7 Q is any valid bound; only the OPTIMAL Q equals inf sigma(A) (the body sentence 'these lower bounds represent the lowest eigenvalues' is exact only for optimal bounds -- FFR 1204.3570 p. 12 shows the Fewster-Eveson 4D bound is ~9x weaker than the estimated optimal one)
hypothesis_drift: NONE in the flat theorem C1 (noise.py:165-177): N1 is supplied by H3 (noise.py:156-162, A_tau the Friedrichs extension on Hadamard vectors -- the self-adjoint operator FFR 1204.3570 p. 2 say they mean, 'whose lower bound coincides with the sharpest possible quantum inequality bound'); N2 is met because the tree bounds the FORM on the form domain (noise.py:172-173), which contains D(A) -- a stronger premise, not a weaker one; N3 is H6 verbatim (noise.py:164-168); only (a)=>(b)=>(c) is used, not N6. The chain is used exactly as published.

WEAKENED (the domain / self-adjoint-realisation hypothesis N1+N2) in the CURVED application: noise.py:42-44 and ledger.py:1822-1826 (O2 row; LEDGER.md:111) apply note [18] to 'an absolute QEI evaluated on the corridor' without naming that the corridor's sampled operator must be realised self-adjointly with the absolute QEI holding on ALL of its domain. H3 as defined (noise.py:156-162) is the Minkowski statement ('smeared Wick-ordered operator on Hadamard vectors', 'C1 is about the Friedrichs extension'); Fewster-Smith gr-qc/0702056, the tree's RIGHT_INSTRUMENT (fewsterteo.py:181-183), bounds Hadamard states, so a curved analogue of H3 (Friedrichs extension from the corridor's Hadamard vectors, or those vectors a form core) is needed and is not stated at these two sites. ledger.py:584-597 (D22 row) does append 'Or a failure of H3 ... a self-adjoint extension other than Friedrichs need not keep the bound', which carries the hypothesis there, but under a flat-space H3 label. Rederive E1-E5 shows the failure mode is real: -d^2/dx^2 on (0,oo) has form >= 0 on C_c^oo but its Robin extension psi'(0)=a psi(0), a<0, has eigenvalue -a^2 < 0.

ADDED/OVERSTATED (a sharpness the note does not supply) in the word 'decides': noise.py:42-44 ('an absolute QEI evaluated on the corridor decides the distribution question there with no variance at all') and ledger.py:584-585 ('by FFR 1004.0179 note [18] it decides the distribution question there'). Note [18] with a non-optimal bound Q gives only supp mu_psi in [-Q,oo): it decides Prob(outcome <= -D) = 0 when D > Q, and decides NOTHING when D <= Q (rederive D1-D3: with inf sigma = -1 and a valid bound Q = 2, D = 0.5 has true probability 1/3, D = 1.5 has 0; the bound is silent on both). Sharpness (N6) is Minkowski-vacuum only and even there is sharpness of inf sigma, not of a given QEI's value. The corridor's absolute QEI is NOT evaluated (fewsterteo.py:149 O2_CLOSED = False; fewsterteo.py:184-187 blocked on the mode functions), so which case obtains is unknown. ledger.py:1822-1826's own wording ('supported in the spectrum of the sampled operator, which an absolute QEI bounds below') is exact and carries no overstatement; the DOCKET 64 comment at ledger.py:1820-1821 already fixed 'bounded BELOW ... not equal to it'.

NOT drift, recorded for completeness: 'every measurement distribution mu_psi is supported in sigma(A_tau)' (noise.py:175-176) holds for every normalised psi in the Hilbert space (and every density matrix), not only psi in D(A) -- the tree's reading is if anything narrower than what the spectral theorem gives.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (31 checks). A1-A4 z3 (unsat of the negation): (b)=>(c) for every normalised psi, (c)=>(a), (a) at eigenvectors =>(b), and (forall psi: <A> >= -Q)=>(b), for a 3-level observable in its eigenbasis; guards A5/A6 show premises satisfiable and (c) falsifiable (no vacuity); A7 z3 finds the note's own caveat as a model (single-psi (c) with sigma not in [-Q,oo)). B: 40 random Hermitian matrices (n=2..6) x 20 states at 30 digits -- Rayleigh quotient >= inf sigma, mu_psi carried by the eigenvalues with mean = <psi,A psi>, Prob(<= -D) = 0 for D > -inf sigma; max residual 4.7e-30 (finite-dimensional ILLUSTRATION of the spectral theorem, not a proof for unbounded A). C: psi orthogonal to the lowest eigenvector gives inf supp = 1 > inf sigma = -2 (note's caveat). D1-D3: a valid non-optimal bound decides P = 0 only for D > Q. E1-E5 (sympy, exact): -d^2/dx^2 on (0,oo) has form >= 0 on a compactly supported core but its Robin extension has eigenvalue -a^2 < 0 -- why N1/N2 (the self-adjoint operator's own domain, i.e. the tree's H3) are load-bearing. F1-F9: the paper's own closed forms re-derived: eq.(24) bound c/(24 pi tau^2), eq.(18) G2 = c/(24 pi^2 tau^4), shifted-Gamma mean 0 and variance G2, P(negative) = 0.8946 / 0.843 / 0.9496 (paper 0.89 / 0.84 / 0.95), Table I moments 1,0,2,48,1740,83904,5051640,364724928,30707616912 reproduced exactly from eq.(26). later_literature.ref: Fewster, Ford, Roman, 'Probability distributions for quantum stress tensors in four dimensions', arXiv:1204.3570 (PRD 85, 125038, 2012)
later_literature.what: Sec. I p. 2: the smeared normal-ordered operators are 'defined, in the first instance, only as symmetric operators on a dense domain' and may have more than one self-adjoint extension; the Friedrichs extension is distinguished, 'whose lower bound coincides with the sharpest possible quantum inequality bound. It is this operator that we have in mind'; whether they are essentially self-adjoint 'is nontrivial and not fully resolved'; distinct extensions share vacuum moments. This is the source of the tree's H3 and makes explicit the N1 hypothesis note [18] states only as 'A is a self-adjoint operator'. p. 3 restates the (b)=>(c) and Reeh-Schlieder parts; p. 12 shows a non-optimal (Fewster-Eveson) bound 27/128 against an estimated optimal 0.0236 -- the N7 gap between a QEI and inf sigma; p. 20 'the conclusion that the probability distribution has a lower bound is independent of any concerns about uniqueness, because this follows from existing quantum inequality bounds'.

later_literature.ref: Fewster & Hollands, 'Probability distributions for the stress tensor in conformal field theories', arXiv:1805.04281 (2018)
later_literature.what: p. 3 eq. (1.5): 'on general grounds [12], the infimum of the support is equal to the optimal quantum energy inequality' (inf over a dense core of states); p. 6: in 2D CFT the smeared stress tensor is self-adjoint on D(L_0) with a common core, so there the N1 question is settled; pp. 19 and 21: 'As is required on general grounds, the QEI bound therefore coincides with the infimum of the support' for two new infinite families of samplers. No correction to 1004.0179.

lacked_data: Note [18] is a theorem of operator theory: its conclusion depends on no measured quantity, so there is no datum the authors could have lacked that would move it -- M's hypothesis has no purchase on the equivalence itself, and that is evidence, not presumption: the published text contains no numerical input (READ), and z3 discharges the three implications with Q, the spectrum and the state weights all free (A1-A4). What came LATER is mathematical, not empirical: FFR 1204.3570 (2012) made explicit that the self-adjoint realisation of the smeared operator is not unique in general ('not fully resolved') and that the Friedrichs extension is the one whose lower bound is the sharp QEI -- the tree already carries this as H3, LOAD-BEARING. Fewster-Hollands 1805.04281 (2018) settled self-adjointness for 2D CFT and re-confirmed support-infimum = optimal QEI on two new families. The one number the tree feeds through the note (Q at b = 1 m) moves by 6.13e-10 relative between the tree's rounded HBAR and the exact SI-2019 value: no effect on 71.256. So: no lacked datum changes the conclusion; the only gap is a hypothesis the tree's curved rows leave implicit (see drift), not a datum.
grade_evidence: The theorem itself STANDS exactly as published: READ in full at source (1004.0179v2 pp. 8-9), the three implications machine-checked by z3 with vacuity guards (A1-A7), illustrated at 30 digits on random Hermitian operators (B), the note's caveat reproduced (C), and the paper's own closed forms re-derived exactly (F1-F9); later literature (1204.3570, 1805.04281, READ) confirms it and corrects nothing. Its use in the FLAT theorem C1 (noise.py:165-177) is exact: self-adjointness via H3, the form bound on the form domain, H6 = mu_psi, only (a)=>(b)=>(c). The grade is NARROWED -- not STANDS -- only because of the CURVED application at noise.py:42-44, ledger.py:584-585 and ledger.py:1822-1826 / LEDGER.md:111: (i) 'an absolute QEI ... decides the distribution question' holds only on the smaller class D > Q_corr (the evaluated bound), since a non-optimal bound gives support in [-Q_corr,oo) and nothing sharper (rederive D3: valid bound, true probability 1/3, bound silent); sharpness (N6) is Minkowski-vacuum only; and (ii) note [18] needs the bound on the whole domain of a self-adjoint realisation, which on the corridor is a curved analogue of H3 that these sites do not name (Fewster-Smith bounds Hadamard states; rederive E shows a different extension can lose the bound). Neither point is a refutation and neither is decided against the tree: Q_corr is uncomputed (fewsterteo.py:149 O2_CLOSED = False), and ledger.py:1822-1826's own sentence ('supported in the spectrum ..., which an absolute QEI bounds below') is exact. Nothing here is WRONG; no misprint was found in note [18].
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the curved rows state the two conditions -- 'decides, PROVIDED the evaluated absolute bound Q_corr satisfies D > Q_corr, for the Friedrichs extension of the corridor's sampled operator from its Hadamard vectors (a curved H3)' -- or O2 is closed with Q_corr computed below D and the curved H3 named. To a sharper NARROWED (a demonstrated gap, still not WRONG of FFR): the corridor's absolute QEI evaluated with Q_corr >= D, in which case note [18] decides nothing there. To WRONG: only a self-adjoint A with (a) on all of D(A) and sigma(A) not in [-Q,oo) -- which z3 (A4) and the spectral theorem exclude; none is known.
